title: Waves Cost Schema
description: The token-cost snapshot of one unit of work (w6 Phase 8 — the ECONOMIC sensor, design_principle #13, blueprint capability 'self-instrumentation' lens c). One cost.json is CO-LOCATED in a logbook's directory (location IS the semantics, dp#11): waves/<wN>/logbooks/<slug>/cost.json holds, per primary objective, the tokens consumed (cache vs normal) and a USD figure FROZEN at capture time; the per-primary figures SUM to the logbook total. A diverged_work gets the same file with a single total (no primaries). Written by an odometer hook at each primary-completion (it reads the session transcript's message.usage + the subagents' transcripts, subtracts the last checkpoint, attributes the delta). USD is frozen — not recomputed at read — because the point is a per-release historical snapshot: 'creating a logbook cost 30% fewer tokens in 3.1 than in 3.0' is both a sales line and an optimization compass. Tokens are the immutable fact (they measure framework efficiency, isolated from Anthropic's pricing); USD is the frozen translation.
$comment: CANONICAL SHAPE: a single object with keys generated_at, waves_version, currency, pricing_ref, per_primary, total. OPEN (never additionalProperties:false, dp#11) — a recurring extra key is a signal for the corpus miner, not an error. STOP: one unit of work per file (one logbook, or one diverged_work). INVARIANT: sum(per_primary[].usd) == total.usd and the same per token field — the odometer writes both, the reader never recomputes (USD is frozen). REDIRECT: the BEHAVIOR of what was invoked lives in the usage telemetry logs, not here; the ANALYSIS of the artifacts lives in corpus-insights.json, not here; the pricing TABLE lives in pricing.json (this file only REFERENCES it via pricing_ref). An undeclared sibling field signals you are writing the wrong artifact. bad: putting a per-command heat map here (that is /waves:usage). good: per_primary[] each {tokens cache+normal, frozen usd} summing to total.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the last odometer write to this file.

waves_version.description: The Waves plugin version in effect when this cost was captured (from plugin.json). The KEY that makes a cost comparable across releases — 'the same operation cost less in the newer version'.
waves_version.$comment: STOP: one version string. REDIRECT: it is the version of WAVES, not of the user's product. bad: the product's app version. good: '3.0.11'.

currency.description: ISO currency of the frozen usd figures. Default 'USD'.

pricing_ref.description: Identifier of the pricing.json table snapshot used to freeze the USD (e.g. 'pricing.json@2026-06'). Makes the frozen USD reproducible and auditable.
pricing_ref.$comment: STOP: one reference to the pricing table version. REDIRECT: the actual per-model rates live in pricing.json, not here — this only names which snapshot was applied. bad: inlining the price-per-million numbers here. good: 'pricing.json@2026-06'.

per_primary.description: One entry per primary objective of the logbook, in id order — the 'items of the trip' (each primary = hotel/flight/food, NOT the per-subagent fuel). The subagents and hooks a primary triggered are SUMMED INTO that primary, not broken out. Empty for a diverged_work (which has no primaries — its cost is in total).

total.description: The cost of the whole unit of work — the SUM of per_primary (for a logbook) or the single cost (for a diverged_work). This is 'what the vacation cost'.
total.$comment: STOP: one total = the sum of per_primary (logbook) or the lone cost (diverged_work). INVARIANT: total.usd == sum(per_primary[].usd) and likewise per token field, when per_primary is non-empty. REDIRECT: do not store a roadmap/project rollup here — /waves:cost computes those by aggregating many cost.json files. bad: a project-wide total in one logbook's file. good: this logbook's own total.

usd.description: Frozen total USD (null if no pricing.json was available at capture — tokens are still recorded).

tokens.description: The four billed token types. The cache vs normal split is what yields REAL cost: cache_read bills at ~0.1x and cache_creation at ~1.25x of input, so a naive total x input-price overstates ~10x.
tokens.$comment: STOP: the four counts only — input, output, cache_creation, cache_read. REDIRECT: the USD derived from these belongs in the sibling `usd`, not here; the rates belong in pricing.json. bad: adding a 'usd' inside tokens. good: {input, output, cache_creation, cache_read} as integers.

cost_entry.description: The frozen cost of one primary objective: its tokens (cache vs normal) and frozen USD, including everything that primary triggered (implementation turns + the subagents/hooks it spawned), summed.
cost_entry.$comment: STOP: one primary's cost — tokens + frozen usd + its id/label for traceability. REDIRECT: do not break out per-subagent or per-turn detail (that is the 'fuel of the plane' — out of scope for the high-level snapshot); the WHY of the primary lives in the logbook, not here. bad: a nested per-subagent cost array. good: {primary_id, label, tokens, usd}.

primary_id.description: The main objective id this cost is attributed to.

label.description: Short echo of the primary's content, for reading the file without cross-referencing the logbook.

usd.description: Frozen USD for this primary (null if no pricing.json at capture).
